removed: Suppose the annual report discloses sales of 260, cost of sales of 165 and the opening and closing working-capital balances, while the collection and purchase totals are hidden. Under Northstar's explicit no-write-off, no-acquisition and no-currency-effect scope, the three bridges are \begin{align} 35&=20+260-C,\label{eq:ns-ar}\\ 20&=30+P-165,\\ 30&=20+P-S. \end{align} Here $C$ denotes collections, $P$ purchases and $S$ supplier payments, all in currency units over the same year. Substitution gives $C=245$, $P=155$ and $S=145$. These are identifiable aggregate movements within this model. They do not identify which invoice was paid on which day. If acquisitions or write-offs are admitted, their movement variables enter the same bridges and these totals may cease to be unique.

P begins with cash 500, investments 80 in each subsidiary and an external financial-guarantee liability 6, so its equity is 654. B has cash 300, customer deposits 200 and equity 100. I has cash 200, insurance liability 100 and equity 100. Of I's cash,20 is a demand deposit at B; the same deposit is included in B's liability 200. The deposit is identified by its creditor I, debtor B, currency, amount and matching closing dates. No interest or movement occurs in it during these two periods. Opening FX is 1 USD per FCU.

For P, the guarantee beneficiary is an unrelated external creditor. A supported scope finding places this contract under IFRS~9. Its opening recognized amount is 6. Supported service income is 2 in each period, while independently supplied expected-credit-loss measurements are 7 and 3. Let \(U_t\) be the unamortized initial amount and \(A_t\) that allowance. Subsequent liability is \begin{equation} G_t=\max\{U_t,A_t\},\qquad U_1=4,\quad U_2=2. \label{eq:sector-guarantee-higher-of} \end{equation} This is the higher-of rule in IFRS~9.4.2.1(c), conditional on the stated classification and measurements \citep{eu20231803}. It gives liabilities 7 and 3. The excess above \(U_t\) is 3 and 1, respectively. Its changes,3 and \(-2\), are impairment expense and reversal. Subtracting them from service income 2 gives guarantee profit \(-1\) and 4. No guarantee settlement occurs during these periods, and consolidation does not remove an external liability.

The customer cases separate earned revenue from billing and cash. The cost side requires a second history: which goods and asset components remain, what they cost, and which losses or revaluations they have already absorbed. Ordinary cost and replacement cases establish that history before production and changed obligations make it more complex.

These cost, benefit and obligation measurements supply the starting states for the following changes. Production first asks which costs the output can carry; later examples change estimates, rights and obligations while retaining their earlier measurement histories.

Ordinary employee benefits and impairment have established how service and past measurements remain in state. Share awards add settlement choices and vesting conditions; the valuation and capitalization methods that follow address the inputs and costs those cases require. These extensions retain the historical EU source scope stated with the earlier foundations.
